blockers.message: the review record has no `## plan.challenge` section, while roles were active at it
R-security-1 (Path traversal in read_attachment through the client-supplied name) is high and still open; fix it, or a human accepts the risk or defers it

findings.evidence:
path = os.path.join(UPLOAD_DIR, str(ticket_id), name)
with open(path, "rb") as f:
findings.recommendation: CWE-22. An agent allowed to read ticket 1 calls read_attachment with name "../2/invoice.pdf" and gets another ticket's attachment, bypassing may_read_ticket; with "../../../../etc/passwd", or an absolute name such as "/etc/passwd" (os.path.join discards the base), it reads any file the service can read. Validate the name where it enters: reject anything that is not equal to os.path.basename(name), or empty, "." or "..", or better look it up in the attachments table for that ticket_id; then resolve the path with os.path.realpath and check it stays under UPLOAD_DIR/<ticket_id> before opening it.
findings.title: Path traversal in read_attachment through the client-supplied name

findings.evidence: def save_attachment(ticket_id: int, filename: str, data: bytes) -> str:
findings.recommendation: CWE-862. Unlike read_attachment, the upload takes no agent id and checks nothing, so any caller can attach files to (or overwrite same-named files of) any ticket, unless the unseen caller checks it. Take the agent id and enforce the write permission on the server here, as read_attachment does with may_read_ticket.
findings.title: save_attachment enforces no authorization on the ticket
